title: Winlink, gateways and mesh networks
idea: Winlink is email by radio: connect to a gateway on its published frequency, over VHF packet or HF with PACTOR or VARA. An AREDN mesh carries high-speed data and routes around a failed node.

rows: Radio email, can be packet, VHF and HF: all of these
A digital protocol used with Winlink
Connect message on its published frequency
High-speed data in an emergency or community event
Packets can go via an alternate node

compare.how: Email over radio through a gateway, on VHF or HF.
High-speed microwave data network that heals around failures.
Digital voice, not email or data networks.

traps.wrong: Respond when the station broadcasts its SSID
traps.why: Gateways don't call out; you transmit a connect request on their published frequency.
A TNC is the modem at your end; the Remote Message Server is the gateway.

traps.wrong: A low signal-to-noise digital mode used for EME (moonbounce)
traps.why: VARA is the protocol Winlink uses, not a moonbounce mode.

traps.wrong: To provide FM repeater coverage in remote areas
traps.why: AREDN carries high-speed data, not FM repeater coverage.

traps.wrong: Having more nodes increases signal strengths
traps.why: More nodes give more routes, not stronger signals.

traps.wrong: Winlink, PACTOR II, and PACTOR III
traps.why: Winlink and PACTOR carry email and files, not voice.
